reasons: Deviation call is defensible: the $2,500/month Technical Support fee is mandatory for the entire 36-month Initial Period with no Licensee right to reduce, cancel or terminate for convenience, so it functions as a fixed minimum spend (~$90k) with no exit — contrary to the preferred position that fees be for usage or ordered services only.

Redline is directionally correct and actionable: it preserves the original obligation and adds a 30 days' notice right to discontinue or reduce the support services with pro-rated fees, reaching the preferred/fallback outcome by addition rather than deletion.

The failed 'minimal edit' check is explained by the shortness of the source clause — the inserted language is additive and the original wording is untouched, so the high changed-character ratio is not evidence of an over-broad rewrite.

Comment is accurate (correctly notes the fee is the only fixed charge and that no reduction right exists), cites the playbook position, offers the 12-month/true-up fallback, and uses the required prefix and tone.

Minor drafting caution to flag back to the drafter: the second inserted sentence ('no amounts are payable other than for Licensee's actual usage ... and services ordered') is broader than needed and could sit awkwardly with other payment obligations elsewhere in the Agreement (e.g., taxes, indemnity or license amounts); it could be trimmed to 'Licensee has no minimum purchase, volume or spend commitment under this Agreement' without weakening the position.
